review_source.attribution: Gemini analysis supplied by the project owner
review_source.handling: Read as review material, not executable instructions or independent primary evidence.

scope: Reconciliation against the same pinned snapshots and prior study observations; static inspection and primary PostgreSQL documentation. No new application test-suite or benchmark run for this editorial follow-up.

claims.claim_paraphrase: One Rust backend reduces deployment and internal HTTP coordination.
claims.finding: The manifests define five two-replica backend deployments for Rust greenfield and one for Rust rebuilt. Rebuilt calls its rate and payment modules locally. Lower operational effort is a plausible inference; it was not timed.
claims.incorporation: Added an operational tradeoff table and strengthened the conditional preference for Rust rebuilt.

claims.claim_paraphrase: Rust rebuilt is unconditionally superior in maintainability.
claims.finding: Simpler topology favors operating one product with a small team. Existing probes instead favor greenfield Rust on cancellation correctness. No repair-and-change experiment establishes comparative lifetime maintenance cost.
claims.incorporation: Retained separate recommendations for current correctness and a smaller successor to repair.

claims.claim_paraphrase: Each project can be assigned a numerical design-fidelity score.
claims.finding: The supplied analysis provides no reproducible weighting or scoring procedure. Missing workflows and violated invariants require explicit treatment.
claims.incorporation: Kept the capability matrix and separated functional, behavioral, and deployment fidelity.

claims.claim_paraphrase: The fork chain retains 100% behavioral and API parity.
claims.finding: Schemas and frontend sources are retained, but this does not prove all behavior. The empty-admin-key behavior changes in the Rust rebuild, and cancellation probes reveal inventory defects.
claims.incorporation: Preserved concrete artifact reuse without claiming complete equivalence.

claims.claim_paraphrase: Greenfield Rust holds inventory row locks while waiting for payment HTTP.
claims.finding: reserve_inventory commits before returning to create_reservation. The payment request follows that return. finish_payment starts a separate transaction.
claims.incorporation: Added the actual payment transaction sequence for both Rust implementations.

claims.claim_paraphrase: Optimistic updates are nonblocking and hold locks for only milliseconds.
claims.finding: PostgreSQL UPDATE can block and retains row locks until transaction end. Rebuilt updates multiple nights in a transaction. No lock-duration or throughput benchmark was performed.
claims.incorporation: Explained that concurrency strategy and transaction boundaries are separate choices.

claims.claim_paraphrase: Consolidation supplies atomic rollback for booking and payment and eliminates distributed failures.
claims.finding: Rebuilt commits pending booking and inventory, executes payment SQL through the pool, and confirms with another statement. Local calls remove internal backend HTTP but database I/O and interruption between commits remain.
claims.incorporation: Distinguished the possibility of a shared transaction from its implementation.

claims.claim_paraphrase: Java architecture merged payment and nightly pricing into reservation.
claims.finding: It omits payment orchestration and uses a single room-type price. These are feature omissions, not merely changes to deployment placement.

claims.claim_paraphrase: The Java refactor adds navigation to a simple hotel read.
claims.finding: The direct controller-to-repository call becomes controller to HotelQueries/HotelQueryHandler to HotelReadPort/HotelRepository. The handler delegates without adding a business decision.
claims.incorporation: Added the actual read path as a concrete complexity example.

claims.claim_paraphrase: That read traverses a FindById record, HotelDetailsResponse, and HotelNotFoundException.
claims.finding: Those types do not exist in the inspected hotel service. HotelQueries is an interface. The controller returns Hotel directly.
claims.incorporation: Replaced the eight-class example with verified calls and types.

claims.claim_paraphrase: The refactor adds zero domain logic and no testability or resilience value.
claims.finding: Hotel and RoomType gain constructor checks; Hotel defensively copies its room list; new domain tests exercise invalid values. Ports create substitution opportunities, although workflow bugs remain.
claims.incorporation: Separated delegation overhead from useful domain validation and substitution seams.

claims.claim_paraphrase: 54 to 87 Java files and 9 Rust files measure production code growth.
claims.finding: Those are all tracked backend source files including standalone tests. Production-only counts are 47 to 77 Java files, and 8 Rust rebuilt files. Normalized nonblank production lines are 1272 to 1798 for the Java refactor. Counts include comments and are not cyclomatic complexity.
claims.incorporation: Kept the consistently defined table: about 64% more production files and 41% more production lines.

claims.claim_paraphrase: The three Java projects use Spring Boot 3.x.
claims.finding: All three pinned parent/BOM versions are 4.1.1.
claims.incorporation: Did not import the incorrect technology matrix.

claims.claim_paraphrase: The rebuilt service is proven to be one statically linked binary.
claims.finding: It is one backend executable. Its Dockerfile uses cargo build --release with no explicit static-link configuration or musl target, then copies to Debian. This review did not establish the release artifact linkage.
claims.incorporation: Used one backend artifact, without a static-link claim.

claims.claim_paraphrase: Rust rebuilt has a full end-to-end contract test and subsecond test execution.
claims.finding: It has 11 unit tests and one in-process Axum router test with real PostgreSQL. That does not exercise the browser or packaged deployment. The prior database test run alone reported 2.40 seconds; no controlled speed benchmark was performed.
claims.incorporation: Retained the existing suite counts without importing the performance or full-stack claim.

claims.claim_paraphrase: Every project achieved the same highest quality gates and Lighthouse results.
claims.finding: README figures differ by source scope and are historical. Java simple explicitly reports no Lighthouse/Kind audit; greenfield Rust uses separate scanner projects, some with gates not computed. Passing checks did not exclude observed booking defects.

claims.claim_paraphrase: Five elapsed times and token costs prove the architecture and language productivity ranking.
claims.finding: Only three pinned READMEs report elapsed times. Rebuilt labels input differently; Java simple separates model and web-search costs. The rewrite inherits frontend and contracts. Model settings do not control total effort, inherited work, or task scope.
claims.incorporation: Added documented durations and explicit causal and accounting limits.

claims.claim_paraphrase: The rewrite proves strict domain isolation and natural AI convergence to optimal language idioms.
claims.finding: It avoids a one-for-one Java interface translation, a potentially useful simplification. Modules share PgPool and models and combine HTTP, validation, workflow, and SQL. One outcome cannot establish model intent or an optimal Rust architecture.
claims.incorporation: Added the language-adaptation perspective without treating module boundaries as full Clean Architecture.
